title: Hedge Obstructions and Decision-Window Memory for Identification in Periodic Causal Systems
banked_reason: Math and decision panels pass, but the exact two-track classification and quadratic lower bound leave the arbitrary strict-unit-latency worst-case order unresolved between quadratic and exponential, so the field-floor gate assigns incremental tier.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery independently repaired and validated the cyclic two-track family, proving its exact CRT phase classification, minimum hedge and decision-window depths, and an every-width quadratic lower bound for both exact-one and latency-at-most-one ambient classes. The finite hedge criterion and published periodic cutoff were source-attested, and both math and decision panels passed. What remains is the load-bearing generic theorem: arbitrary strict-unit-latency graphs are still bounded only between quadratic and exponential memory, with no shortening invariant or superquadratic construction available.
tldr: For arbitrary fixed standard-Borel domains, the first active-backdoor boundary gives an observed-law functional before \(r\), and the CRT boundary gives the exact graph-level hedge and decision-window memory. Exact late model-level nonidentification additionally requires nondegenerate fixed domains; explicit witnesses now select two points inside those domains rather than replacing them by binary spaces. Compatible late cases have both a depth-\(d_*\) hedge and a threshold-bridge model pair, including \(d_*=0\); incompatible late cases have no finite hedge but acquire an off-support observed-common-cause model pair at \(\operatorname{lcm}(p,q)\). The pure two-track maximum is exact, while globally \(w^2/4-5\le H_1(w)\le H_{\le1}(w)\le2^w(w+1)^{2w+2}\); the sharp order for arbitrary strict exact-one graphs remains open.
gap: The complete finite hedge criterion says which obstruction matters, and Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman prove an exponential generic periodic cutoff, but the minimum backward depth for fixed horizon-one queries is not characterized. Their published lower result varies the future outcome distance rather than the past depth of a witness.
fill: Establish or refute the compatible/incompatible CRT classification by proving an explicit threshold hedge and a universal first-crossing lower bound, derive the quadratic width lower bound, and formalize a compact family-specific decision certificate without claiming a generic polynomial algorithm or functional.
